nodes.name: Nightly at 02:15 UTC
nodes.notes: 02:15 UTC, not midnight: tenants span timezones, so this must run late enough that yesterday has closed for the westernmost tenant. The SQL evaluates each day boundary in the tenant's own timezone, so a single run seals the right 24 hours for a business in Leeds and one in Sydney.

nodes.name: Roll up every tenant
nodes.notes:
Empty body = every active tenant, yesterday. Idempotent (upsert on business_id+day), so a retry recomputes rather than double-counting.

10 minute timeout: this is a batch job, not a request path.

nodes.name: Retention sweep
nodes.notes:
Enforces each tenant's data_retention_days. A documented retention period only means something if something actually deletes.

Batched at 5,000 rows per table per night so an unbounded delete never holds locks long enough to affect live traffic; the schedule catches up over successive nights.

meta.description: Seals yesterday's metrics into analytics_daily so trend queries never scan the message log, then runs the GDPR retention sweep. Sequential on purpose — rolling up before deleting means the aggregates survive the data they came from.
